title: Guthrie supports House passage of FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
Guthrie supports House passage of FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act
M. S. Garber
Congressman Brett Guthrie announced on July 22 the House passage of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027. The legislation authorizes $1.15 trillion in discretionary defense spending, aligning with President Trump’s budget request.
Guthrie said, “As a graduate of West Point and former officer in the U.S. Army, I am proud to support this year’s NDAA, which ensures America’s heroes have the tools and support necessary to carry out their mission.” He continued, “This legislation unleashes America’s private defense manufacturing capabilities and invests in much-needed quality of life improvements for our servicemembers. This bill is a win for our military and national security, plain and simple.”
The act allocates funds across several categories: $258 billion for procurement of new equipment; $219 billion for research, development, test, and evaluation; $247 billion for military personnel and health; $338 billion for operation and maintenance; $28 billion for military construction and family housing; and $41 billion toward defense nuclear programs. It also provides a pay raise between five percent to seven percent for all servicemembers.
The bill directs resources to strengthen nuclear deterrence, expand missile defense capabilities, counter threats from adversaries such as China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, expand domestic defense manufacturing capacity through statutory reforms, authorize nearly $1 billion to counter drug trafficking efforts, and grant the National Guard authority to procure equipment specifically for counter-narcotics operations.
Brett Guthrie has served in the U.S. Congress representing Kentucky's 2nd District since 2009 after replacing Ron Lewis that year, according to Congressman Guthrie's office. He previously served in the Kentucky Senate from 2000 to 2008.
